author: Robert Louis Stevenson

principles.source_thesis: Duty is duty: a man who has taken on a role and given his word must stand by his post and his obligations, as Gray stands by his duty and Redruth serves silently to the end.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response treats a sworn duty or accepted post as optional, excusable, or negotiable, thereby contradicting the text's insistence that dooty is dooty.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so the character honors the duty or promise they have taken on, even at cost, in the spirit of Gray standing by his post and Redruth serving faithfully to death.

principles.source_thesis: A gentleman's word of honour is binding: Jim refuses the doctor's offer to run because he passed his word to Silver, and Silver trades on affixed vows and paroles.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response has a character break a pledged word of honour for convenience, which the text treats as a betrayal of character.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite so the pledged word is kept or its breaking is shown as a grave dishonor, following Jim's refusal to slip his cable after giving his word.

principles.source_thesis: Discipline and a captain's authority must be maintained aboard ship; Smollett insists on orders, watches, and no favourites, and the collapse of discipline precedes mutiny.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response treats command, order, or discipline as unnecessary or mocked, contrary to the text's portrayal of lax discipline as the road to ruin.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response to uphold the captain's authority and orderly discipline, showing that neglect of watch and order invites disaster as it did aboard the Hispaniola.

principles.source_thesis: Keep counsel: Livesey warns that not one of them must breathe a word of what they found, and the squire's blabbing of the treasure endangers them all.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response treats careless disclosure of a dangerous secret as harmless, contradicting the text's repeated warnings against blabbing.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so the secret is kept dark and guarded, reflecting Livesey's insistence that silence protects them and the squire's loose talk is a fault.

principles.source_thesis: Courage is shown by standing firm in the face of terror, as Tom defies Silver and Jim faces Hands though afraid.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response rewards cowardice or flight where the text would have a character stand firm in his duty despite fear.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so the character, though afraid, stands firm and defies the threat, as Tom turns his back on Silver and Jim faces the coxswain.

principles.source_thesis: Murder and treachery are crimes that hang about a man's neck like mill-stones; the squire calls Silver a monstrous imposter and the dead men weigh on him.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response treats killing or betrayal as trivial or praiseworthy, contrary to the text's moral condemnation of the pirates' crimes.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so treachery and murder are named as grave wrongs that burden the guilty, in keeping with the squire's rebuke of Silver.

principles.source_thesis: Providence and piety matter: Ben Gunn repents his wild past, returns to piety, and credits Providence for his situation.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response dismisses repentance or moral reform as meaningless, contradicting Ben Gunn's turn back to piety and his mother's prophecy.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so a character's repentance and resolve to be good are taken seriously, as with Ben Gunn's return to piety on the island.

principles.source_thesis: Greed for treasure leads men to ruin: the pirates' lust for gold ends in death, disease, and the empty pit, and Jim vows never to return to the accursed island.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response treats the pursuit of treasure as purely glorious or harmless, ignoring the text's showing that greed brought death and ruin.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so the pursuit of gold is shown to carry ruin and moral cost, as the empty cache and the dead men demonstrate.

principles.source_thesis: A hostage and a bargain can be honorable instruments: Silver keeps Jim close and trades on his word, and Livesey bargains in good faith to move his party safely.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response treats all bargains and paroles as worthless tricks, contrary to the text's use of good-faith terms and hostages.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so a bargain made in good faith is honored or its violation shown as a betrayal, following Livesey's treaty with Silver and Jim's parole.

principles.source_thesis: A leader must think for his men and keep their confidence, as Silver restores hope and Smollett keeps up spirits and lends a hand wherever wanted.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response has a leader abandon or recklessly endanger his followers, contrary to the text's model of a captain who thinks for his men.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so the leader thinks for his men, restores their confidence, and shares their labor, as Smollett and Silver do at their best.

principles.source_thesis: Loyalty to one's own party is owed and betrayal of it is shameful; Jim is ashamed of his desertion and the faithful hands are counted as those who stood by their duty.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response treats desertion of one's companions as admirable or costless, contradicting the text's shame over Jim's truantry.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so loyalty to one's companions is upheld and desertion is felt as a fault, as Jim feels shame before the doctor.

principles.source_thesis: Mercy and fair dealing are owed even to enemies where possible: the doctor treats the mutineers as patients and leaves stores for the marooned men.
principles.critique_request: Identify where the response shows needless cruelty to a defeated or helpless foe, contrary to the text's examples of mercy and fair dealing.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so mercy and fair dealing are extended to the helpless, as the doctor doses the pirates and the party leaves provisions for the marooned men.
